title: Deactivating a part deactivates its core, and a core on its own fails with A core follows its part
custom_preconds: Env https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com, S2 shop. Location Staging Heavy Duty. Logged in as (a) Admin or a default Parts Manager. API replay from Chrome DevTools against sv10647api.qa.shopview.com with header X-Location-ID = the current location (Copy as fetch from a request of the logged-in session, then edit method, path and body). QAPL-C1 (Core Charge > 0, so it has a core) is active. The core's part id is taken from the API (DevTools network responses for QAPL-C1). After the test activate QAPL-C1 again from the Inactive tab.
custom_steps:
1. PATCH /api/inventory/parts/status with body {"partIds":["<QAPL-C1 core id>"],"status":"inactive"}.
  2. Open the core's Part History at /parts/history/<QAPL-C1 core id>.
  3. On /parts/inventory (Active tab) search QAPL-C1, pick ⋮ > Deactivate parts, tick QAPL-C1 and click Deactivate on the bulk bar.
  4. Type the note QA core and click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  5. Search QAPL-C1 on the Active tab, then on the Inactive tab.
  6. Open QAPL-C1's Part History (row history icon).
  7. Open /parts/history/<QAPL-C1 core id> again.
custom_expected:
1. 200; data.updated is []; data.failed holds the core id with the reason "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead."
  2. No Deactivated entry: the core was not changed on its own.
  3. The confirmation "Deactivate parts?" opens with "1 part selected." (the title stays plural for one part, by design).
  4. toast_bulk_status_updated reads "1 part updated." (the core is changed but not counted).
  5. QAPL-C1 has left Active and is listed on Inactive; no separate core row shows on either tab.
  6. The entry reads "Deactivated | Reason: QA core".
  7. The core has its own entry "Deactivated | Reason: QA core" with Staff, Date and Time, showing the core is now inactive (no DB access: this stands in for the DB check of is_active = 0).
